question: Why is Nikolsky's sign positive in pemphigus vulgaris but negative in bullous pemphigoid?

answers.text: In pemphigus, anti-desmoglein antibodies weaken adhesion between keratinocytes (intra-epidermal), so tangential pressure shears the surface; in pemphigoid, the keratinocytes remain firmly bound and only the deeper sub-epidermal junction is attacked, so the surface holds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Nikolsky's sign tests epidermal cohesion. In pemphigus, anti-desmoglein 3/1 IgG disrupts desmosomal adhesion holding keratinocytes together (intra-epidermal), so lateral pressure makes the upper epidermis slide off. In pemphigoid, anti-BP180/BP230 attacks the deeper hemidesmosomal anchorage, leaving keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion intact.

answers.text: Pemphigus causes a sub-epidermal split while pemphigoid is intra-epidermal, making pemphigus skin more fragile at the surface

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This reverses the split levels. Pemphigus is intra-epidermal (anti-desmoglein), pemphigoid is sub-epidermal (anti-BP180/BP230). Getting the split level correct is the key to understanding why the signs differ.

answers.text: Pemphigoid antibodies target desmoglein while pemphigus antibodies target BP180, producing opposite mechanical effects

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The antibody targets are reversed. Pemphigus targets desmogleins (desmosomal proteins between keratinocytes); pemphigoid targets BP180/BP230 (hemidesmosomal proteins anchoring epidermis to dermis).

answers.text: The sign depends on blood pressure rather than structural adhesion, and pemphigus patients have higher cutaneous blood pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nikolsky's sign has nothing to do with blood pressure. It tests the mechanical integrity of adhesion within the epidermis by applying tangential shear force to the skin surface.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key: Nikolsky tests intra-epidermal cohesion. In pemphigus, anti-desmoglein IgG loosens keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte binding (intra-epidermal) so the surface shears. In pemphigoid, anti-BP180/BP230 IgG attacks the sub-epidermal anchor but the epidermis above stays bound.
Correct — anti-desmoglein antibodies in pemphigus weaken the epidermis internally so it shears, while anti-BP180/BP230 in pemphigoid attacks the deeper junction and leaves the surface intact.
